security.heading: When should your computer ask for your password?
security.text: Some settings (such as installing programs) ask for your password. That way nobody can change your computer without you knowing.
security.all: Ask for every change (the most secure)
security.recommended: Only for risky things: disks, users, startup (more convenient)
security.not_admin: Only an administrator account can change this.
security.autologin: Sign in automatically: start straight to the desktop without a password
security.later: You can fine-tune this later in Sloth Center (Account and security).
sharing.heading: Help Windows programs start on the first try for everyone
sharing.text: When you start a Windows program or game, Sloth OS finds the setting that works for it on its own. If you allow it, we share the working setting anonymously, so it starts on the first try on other Sloth OS computers too.
sharing.what: Only this is sent: the setting (for example "older graphics mode"), your graphics card's manufacturer, and a fingerprint of the program that its name cannot be recovered from. Nothing else leaves your computer: not your name, not your files, not the program's name, and not when or how much you use it.
sharing.later: You can change this any time later in Sloth Center (Windows programs). You get the settings that worked on other computers either way.
windows.heading: Bring your files over from Windows?
windows.text: This computer also has Windows. We can copy your files over; Windows itself isn't touched, we only read from it.
windows.bookmarks: Browser bookmarks (into one file on the Desktop that your browser can import)
windows.onedrive: Your OneDrive files are available in Sloth Center, under Account and security → Cloud storage.
windows.done: Done: {count} files from Windows are here.
windows.failed_some: {count} files couldn't be copied (e.g. damaged or locked files).
windows.nospace: Not enough free space: {need} needed, {free} free. Choose fewer folders.
windows.locked: The Windows drive is encrypted (BitLocker), so it can't be read. If you need your files, turn off BitLocker in Windows, or copy them to a USB stick.
windows.none: No Windows files to bring over were found on this computer.
windows.failed: The Windows drive couldn't be opened. Start Windows and shut it down completely (Shut down, not Restart), then try again from Sloth Center (Disks).
